source.title: Are Single-Token Sparse Autoencoder Features Causally Necessary? Layer-Depth and SAE-Family Effects
source.authors: Seonglae Cho; Ze-Kun Wu; Kleyton da Costa; Rishi Kalra; Ilham Wicaksono; A. Koshiyama

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the paper and appendices through Table 27; no garbling or cutoff is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests causal roles of SAE features in language models and reports that those roles differ across SAE families, refining and challenging the idea that SAE features are stable, portable units. It does not reproduce the original toy-model method.
record.gate_note: The paper measures single-token-feature prevalence, geometry, and causal effects in language models. Rows below focus on results relevant to sparse SAE features and their causal stability. The paper also reports many token categories, layerwise p-values, and ancillary alignment and persistence analyses that do not directly test the listed claim versions; these are not recorded as separate rows.
record.test_reason: The study zero-ablates SAE features in six pretrained LMs against matched controls (bears on V4). It compares token-matched features across SAE families and recipes on the same base model, showing causal roles differ by SAE (bears on V5, argues it needs restating). No toy models, neuron polysemanticity or feature-dimensionality tests.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Add three points. Single-token feature ablation lowers the target logit in 178/208 layers. The same token can be causally anchored under one SAE family and locally redundant under another. Because changing only the activation function flips the sign of the difference, the authors name training recipe as the residual candidate and urge treating SAE family as an experimental variable.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes pretrained language-model SAEs and performs decoder-feature zero-ablation, geometry measurements, and cross-family comparisons; the cited original concerns toy models of superposition. No direct reproduction of the original toy-model recipe is reported.
record.method_sensitivity: The results vary with SAE family and training methodology; prevalence varies with model scale; causal effect size varies by layer depth and model. The paper reports that the activation-function-controlled comparison reverses the direction seen in the token-matched family comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: Single-token SAE features cluster 4.7× tighter in decoder space and align more with token embeddings (0.67 vs 0.39).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Token-identity SAE features form a geometrically distinct, embedding-aligned subpopulation of decoder directions.

fits_no_version.finding: Single-token feature prevalence falls with model scale within the GemmaScope/res-jb family (1.48% → 0.47% → 0.14%, n=3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger LMs' SAEs contain proportionally fewer single-token features.

fits_no_version.finding: Necessity damage rises with depth (ρ up to 0.97) while downstream anchoring concentrates in early layers (ρ=−0.65).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early SAE features act as propagation anchors; late ones shape the output directly.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: Cross-family prevalence comparisons co-vary training data, dictionary width, training recipe, post-hoc conversion, and sometimes base model or tokenizer. The study focuses on single-token features and leaves multi-token and compositional features for future work. The authors note weaker effects for Gemma-3-1B GemmaScope and that the three-point scaling trend cannot distinguish functional forms.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports additional layerwise p-values, token categories, semantic matches, and robustness analyses. These were omitted where they did not add a distinct result for the listed claim versions; the retained causal configuration rows include the main per-configuration significance counts from Table 6.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity transition or superposition geometry.
All: capacity-sharing remarks in Appendix B.2/A.3 are interpretation, not tests on model neurons.
Whether features are spread across many neurons. Whether SAE recovery shows superposition. Features beyond single-token ones.
Completeness of dictionaries. Canonicity beyond single-token features. Multi-token and compositional features (left to future work).
All: intrinsic dimension of the decoder-vector set is not feature dimensionality.

missing.what: Same model, layer and activation function, different recipe: GemmaScope vs community JumpReLU at Gemma-2-2B L1. Degradation median 0.51 vs 2.06 log2, p=3.1e-15.
Token-matched category convergence across GemmaScope vs BatchTopK: 62% overall, code/math 93%, function words 29%. Shows where SAE features are stable.
Sparsity dose-response: TopK k=25→100 changes mean ∆logit −0.152→−0.036; JumpReLU shows no trend. A hyperparameter alters the causal role of the same-token feature.
Single-token prevalence across eight SAE architectures on Gemma-2-2B L12: 0.92–0.99%, but Gated 0.38% and P-Anneal 0.42%.
Alignment-matched null: single-token necessity exceeds nearest-alignment controls at 8/9 layer-configurations, though the controls show a geometric component.
Non-single-token control ablations are inert in every configuration (recovery ≥99.96%).

record.verdict_notes: The abstract says 'on the same base model' when contrasting LlamaScope with GemmaScope/BatchTopK, but LlamaScope runs only on Llama/DeepSeek. The truly within-model evidence is GemmaScope vs BatchTopK on Gemma and the controlled L1 comparisons. Single-token features are close to token embeddings, so V4 support is limited to this easy, embedding-aligned case. The paper is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks with more features than dimensions, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular superposition geometry are tested.
No test of polysemantic neurons arising from competition for limited model dimensions, or of important features receiving dedicated dimensions while others share them.
No test of polysemantic neurons arising through mechanisms other than capacity pressure.
The paper studies single-token SAE features, not whether general features are distributed across many neurons or whether SAE recovery establishes superposition across LLMs.

The paper tests causal portability across SAE families for matched single-token features; it does not establish whether SAE dictionaries are complete or whether features are canonical in every other sense.
The study represents SAE features with decoder vectors but does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional feature representations.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Measured decoder-space clustering of activation-detected single-token features against the polysemantic complement.
rows.measure: Mean pairwise cosine similarity; single-token/polysemantic clustering ratio
rows.note: This is decoder geometry of detected SAE features, not a direct test of superposition in the underlying model.
rows.check: Decoder clustering of selected single-token features vs the polysemantic complement is a detection-validation property. It is not evidence that the LLM contains SAE-recoverable features (V4).

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B and Gemma-3-1B token-matched features
rows.operation_detail: Compared causal measures for token-ID-matched features across GemmaScope and BatchTopK SAEs.
rows.measure: Downstream anchoring, ∆logit-lens
rows.note: A within-base-model matched comparison; recovery did not differ significantly (p = 0.41).
rows.check: Stability of causal role is absent for anchoring (r=0.36, p=1.2e-18). Same table shows recovery does not differ (p=0.41). Not a V4 test.

source_check.correct: State: partial causal stability. Both families show downstream anchoring, but BatchTopK has greater anchoring: 15,537 versus 8,554, p = 1.2 × 10−18, r = 0.36.
source_check.problem: A significant difference in anchoring does not establish that stable causal structure is wholly absent.

rows.operation_detail: Compared causal measures for token-ID-matched features across GemmaScope and BatchTopK SAEs.
rows.measure: Necessity measured by ∆rank
rows.note: The difference is statistically reported, but the effect size is smaller than for the anchoring comparison.
rows.check: Small but significant necessity difference (r=0.12) between families on token-matched features. Not V4.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B, community SAEs
rows.operation_detail: Compared token-matched single-token features under TopK and JumpReLU with controlled model, layer, and dictionary width.
rows.measure: Necessity, mean ∆rank
rows.note: This direction is opposite to the token-matched BatchTopK-versus-GemmaScope comparison; the authors conclude activation function alone does not explain the family differences.
rows.check: Same model, layer and width; only activation function differs. Necessity differs (r=0.20, p=0.036), so stability is only partial. State here is relative to V5's stability claim, not the direction.

rows.subject: GemmaScope/BatchTopK versus LlamaScope configurations

relation.reason: The study reports its own feature measurements, controlled ablations, and within-model SAE comparisons bearing on V4 and V5.

tranche.reason: Same-model token-matched interventions show SAE-dependent causal roles, requiring qualification of V5's strong stability and canonicity claim.

source_check.notes: The authors' 178/208 summary matches Table 6. Appendix B.14 uses nearest-alignment controls with substantial residual cosine gaps; cross-base-model family contrasts should not be described as same-model comparisons.
